{
  "IP": "neorv32_trng",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Generated random data",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "Unpredictable entropy bytes generated by neoTRNG, assembled from sampled cell output and buffered for software reads; the TRNG depends on them to provide random data. The information is generated internally rather than entering through a unit port.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The random bytes can be exposed through the bus response data field at line 117, and random numbers are information an integrator may require to remain confidential. The sampled word is held and updated at line 360 and passed through the generation and FIFO path at lines 366, 139 and 161, so compromise of that path can alter returned entropy. Disabling generation or clearing the FIFO at lines 105, 137 and 170 can prevent entropy from being available, while lines 114-117 can withhold it from a read.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker able to control the bus-facing control path could observe returned entropy or disable and clear the generator path so that reads expose zeros or otherwise fail to provide valid random data.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        360,
        366
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        117
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "TRNG enable control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The runtime control bit that enables sampling and generation and, when cleared, also causes the random FIFO to be cleared; TRNG operation depends on this setting.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The bus write stores this configuration at line 105 and it controls the generator through line 137, so unauthorized modification can change the configured operating mode. Clearing the setting is propagated to sampling and FIFO clearing at lines 354 and 170, which can stop generation and withhold random data.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could issue an unchecked bus write that clears the enable bit, stopping entropy generation and clearing the pool.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        105
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        105
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        109
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "FIFO clear control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The runtime command bit that requests clearing of the buffered random-data pool; the command affects whether already generated entropy remains available. It has no exit port because the RTL does not return this command bit.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The bus write stores the clear command at line 106 and the resulting control drives FIFO clear at line 170, allowing the buffered entropy state to be modified. Activating the clear path at lines 106 and 170 discards pending random data and can prevent a required read from being served.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could write the clear control bit to discard buffered entropy and cause subsequent random-data reads to return no valid data.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        106
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        106
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Random-data availability status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The FIFO status indicating whether generated random data is available; it is used both as software-visible status and to select random data versus zero on a data read.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Under the another-IP black-box rule, the FIFO produces the availability status through line 167, and the RTL uses it to report status at line 112 and to select the returned value at lines 114-117, so corruption can make the interface report or return the wrong result. The same decision controls whether a read returns entropy or zeros at lines 114-117, so a false unavailable state can block the required transfer.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could cause the FIFO availability decision to indicate empty or otherwise be wrong, making the peripheral return zeros or withhold available entropy.",
      "Enters Through": [],

        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],

  ],

conceptual assets.information: Unpredictable entropy bytes generated by neoTRNG, assembled from sampled cell output and buffered for software reads; the TRNG depends on them to provide random data. The information is generated internally rather than entering through a unit port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The random bytes can be exposed through the bus response data field at line 117, and random numbers are information an integrator may require to remain confidential. The sampled word is held and updated at line 360 and passed through the generation and FIFO path at lines 366, 139 and 161, so compromise of that path can alter returned entropy. Disabling generation or clearing the FIFO at lines 105, 137 and 170 can prevent entropy from being available, while lines 114-117 can withhold it from a read.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to control the bus-facing control path could observe returned entropy or disable and clear the generator path so that reads expose zeros or otherwise fail to provide valid random data.

conceptual assets.information: The runtime control bit that enables sampling and generation and, when cleared, also causes the random FIFO to be cleared; TRNG operation depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The bus write stores this configuration at line 105 and it controls the generator through line 137, so unauthorized modification can change the configured operating mode. Clearing the setting is propagated to sampling and FIFO clearing at lines 354 and 170, which can stop generation and withhold random data.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue an unchecked bus write that clears the enable bit, stopping entropy generation and clearing the pool.

conceptual assets.information: The runtime command bit that requests clearing of the buffered random-data pool; the command affects whether already generated entropy remains available. It has no exit port because the RTL does not return this command bit.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The bus write stores the clear command at line 106 and the resulting control drives FIFO clear at line 170, allowing the buffered entropy state to be modified. Activating the clear path at lines 106 and 170 discards pending random data and can prevent a required read from being served.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write the clear control bit to discard buffered entropy and cause subsequent random-data reads to return no valid data.

conceptual assets.information: The FIFO status indicating whether generated random data is available; it is used both as software-visible status and to select random data versus zero on a data read.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Under the another-IP black-box rule, the FIFO produces the availability status through line 167, and the RTL uses it to report status at line 112 and to select the returned value at lines 114-117, so corruption can make the interface report or return the wrong result. The same decision controls whether a read returns entropy or zeros at lines 114-117, so a false unavailable state can block the required transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the FIFO availability decision to indicate empty or otherwise be wrong, making the peripheral return zeros or withhold available entropy.

considered, not kept.reason: The request strobe, direction and register-select address only determine whether and where an access occurs at lines 103, 104, 108 and 171, so Access command fields makes them part of the access rather than a separate piece.
The acknowledge merely copies the request strobe and the error field is tied to a constant at lines 98-99, so handshake-copy and constant-status rules provide no independent information asset.
The counter and its valid pulse only sequence and pace sampling at lines 355, 359 and 367, so Sequencing state and Pacing pulses bar them as independent information.
TRNG_FIFO only fixes the build-time FIFO depth at lines 22 and 147 and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
SIM_MODE is a build-time generic/constant selection at lines 132 and 288-289, so Build-time values excludes it as a runtime conceptual asset.
